Protesters use makeshift shields during a demonstration in Paris, France, on Saturday [Pedro Nunes/Reuters]By Al Jazeera Staff and AFPPublished On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026
Police have fired tear gas at protesters in Paris and Lyon as hundreds of thousands of mostly young people marched across France over the cost of living and the state of the country’s schools.
Saturday’s rallies were the third consecutive weekend of demonstrations in France.
Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4UN experts sound alarm at excessive use of force in French student protestslist 2 of 4France braces for ‘very high risk’ of disorder at Halloween protestslist 3 of 4Italy tightens security as students, unions launch nationwide protestslist 4 of 4Polish police deployed to top court after head judge suspendedend of list
A coalition of youth organisations and unions representing high school and university students said nearly half a million people took part, including 200,000 in Paris. The authorities put the nationwide turnout at 320,000, including 70,000 in the capital.
Marches in the capital began peacefully, but turned violent as protesters gathered near the point where the main march was due to end on Saturday. Bins and street furniture were set alight, and plumes of smoke could be seen rising over the city.
“What we’ve been seeing … is the police firing a lot of tear gas into this crowd,” said Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler, reporting from Paris, adding that her team “had to move out of the way because it was simply too much for us to breathe”.

Coventry City manager Frank Lampard celebrates after the Sunderland match [Chris Radburn/Reuters]By Kevin HandPublished On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026
Joint record Premier League winners Manchester United were plunged to the brink of the relegation zone by their defeat at Chelsea followed by Coventry City’s win against Sunderland.
Ten-man United were beaten 2-0 at Stamford Bridge in the early kickoff in the English top flight, leaving them on their first nine-match winless run since 1986. The Red Devils have already made their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Despite an improved display in the first -half, in which recalled captain Bruno Fernandes spurned one of many key chances, United were beaten by a brilliant solo goal by Morgan Rogers and a penalty converted by Cole Palmer.
Lisandro Martinez was shown a second yellow card for a reckless challenge on Wesley Fofana in an aerial duel from a corner.
United’s day was about to get worse.
Coventry City’s 3-1 home win against Sunderland saw them leapfrog the fallen giants, leaving United just one point and one place outside the relegation zone.
There’s a chance the 20-time English champions, who have won only once in nine league games, could be in the bottom three by the end of Matchweek 9 – a desperate situation for a club widely regarded as the biggest in the country.

Residents search the rubble for belongings following an Israeli strike in the Bureij refugee camp, in the central Gaza Strip, on October 30, 2026 [AFP]By AnadoluPublished On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026
At least four Palestinians in Gaza have been killed as Israel continues to attack the enclave, despite a so-called “ceasefire” that has been in place for over a year.
Israel carried out several attacks in Gaza on Saturday, including shelling the Nuseirat refugee camp, in which Palestinian teacher Diaa Abu al-Rous was killed, al-Awda Hospital confirmed.

Separately, another man, Arafat al-Arair, died after sustaining serious injuries days earlier when Israel struck a vehicle in the Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood, southwest of Gaza City. A medical source at al-Shifa Hospital confirmed his death.
Meanwhile, two girls also died on Saturday from injuries sustained the previous evening when their tent caught fire at a camp for displaced people in al-Mawasi, in Khan Younis. Nasser Medical Complex confirmed their deaths. It is not clear what caused the fire.
At least six Palestinians were killed in Gaza over the past 48 hours, according to the enclave’s Ministry of Health, bringing the number of people killed since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,580.
In its daily statistical report on Saturday, the ministry said another 26 people were injured over the same period.

Brighton inflicted a second straight Premier League defeat on Manchester City with a 1-0 win to close within two points of the leaders on Saturday.
Third-placed Brighton ended their wait for a first-ever away win against City on their 18th attempt to bolster dreams of challenging for the title.

The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have already beaten champions Arsenal convincingly this season to show their title credentials.
Fabian Hurzeler’s men got revenge for defeat to City on penalties in the League Cup on Wednesday.
Hurzeler felt aggrieved at that result after his side twice led at the Etihad and this time held on after Yasin Ayari slotted them into an 11th-minute lead.
Bart Verbruggen was inspired in the Brighton goal to see off a City onslaught after half-time.
But the visitors were well worthy of a famous win and could also have added to their lead when Jack Hinshelwood hit the side netting late on.

Zaman’s entertaining innings and Arafat Minhas’s robust 61 off 31 balls took Pakistan to a winning 331-7 in 48.3 overs, as the Sri Lankan bowlers found it hard to control the wet ball because of dew in Lahore.

San Francisco, California – Three words stretch across the front page of Richard Pan’s campaign website: “Public Health Hero”.
The California paediatrician is part of a wave of public health professionals angling for a seat in the United States Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections.
The American College of Gastroenterology has estimated that as many as 25 physicians could win congressional office this election cycle, a record number that would usher in "a new generation of physician-lawmakers".
But while many of the incumbents are Republicans, experts say there has been a notable rise in the number of Democratic doctors and healthcare workers on the ballot.
Some are competing in the highest-profile races of the year. Abdul El-Sayed, a physician and former public health official, is locked in a close race for Michigan's open Senate seat.
In South Carolina, meanwhile, paediatrician Annie Andrews has turned what would normally be a safe Senate seat for Republicans into a battleground.

A man runs past a mural of Dakar 2026 as Senegal prepares to host the Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympic event to be held in Africa, in Dakar [Misper Apawu/Reuters]By Nicolas HaquePublished On 31 Oct 202631 Oct 2026
Dakar, Senegal – Senegal’s teenage volleyball players were training, giving everything they had. And I could see it in their eyes: the flame, that desire to win.
I was with my daughter and could see the effect it had on her: watching another girl her age play for a team, for a chance at gold, for something bigger than herself.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Olympic flame arrives in Senegal for first ever Olympic event in Africalist 2 of 3The return of Palestinian football: ‘We are a people who must live’list 3 of 3South Africa centre bid in Durban for first Olympic Games on the continentend of list
I saw it again when my daughter helped a young boxer wrap her hands, before the fighter slipped on her gloves and threw a punch few adults could withstand, and when she helped a rowing captain into the water.
There is an ease with which teenagers find one another, a friendliness adults seem to have forgotten.
And so the 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening on the world’s youngest continent on Saturday feels fitting, particularly in this sports-crazy city I call home.
Looking around Dakar, almost everyone looks like an athlete.
Surfers paddle out at dawn. Children play basketball and football in the streets. Teenagers wrestle on beaches; others swim towards Ngor Island at breakneck speed. Construction workers, after a day’s labour, gather not in pubs or bars, but on the beach – to train, laugh and listen to music.
Sport is a way of life, but also a reason to be together.
